answer: Weight should follow locality, not key count. Each identity is pinned to one network vantage point and must answer latency probes from random regions; the probe delta - the RTT fingerprint - cannot be faked in bulk. Clones co-hosted on one box share a single delta, so the cluster collapses to one seat. Scaling means renting real, geographically distinct infrastructure per clone: like a saffron field, no combine harvester exists - every flower is picked by hand, at cost per head. Honest agents answer probes cheaply and climb a terrace of steady locality; the farm buys its own geography.
